Honestly, if you're wanting to get into malware development and malware reverse engineering (specifically in regards to Windows), I think the most important thing you can learn is the concept of a file. 1. What is a file extension? This is pretty obvious, .exe, .pdf, .mp3, etc. 2. How are file extensions handled? This would introduce the idea of the Windows registry and how extension querying is handled vs. the Windows loader 3. Which file extensions (or file types, rather) are used for payload delivery? e.g. .exe, .dll, .xll, .vbs, .ps1, .py, .lua, .docx, .vcproj, etc. The .exe, .dll, (and other native types, like .sys) will be sort of self-explanatory, but the others would introduce different malware delivery mechanisms (malicious files) and potentially wiggle in the concept of payload smuggling. 4. Each of the previous listed file types are different. How are they different? .exe and .dll (and many others) are native to Windows and handled by the Windows loader. Why are the others still considered executable files? This is when you slowly step into interpretive languages and VM dependency (JVM, PVM, etc). Somewhere in this you would eventually stumble into the Windows PE format, how the PE format is different for .NET binaries, how Electron .JS executables act differently, weird stuff like .docx file internals, etc. Basically, I think understanding files and how they're handled is an excellent starting point and sets the stage for what will happen next. pic unrelated

Here is a short frontline summary for June 2026. Although we assessed that Russian forces gained approximately 25 km² in May 2026, we also noted that they may have lost more territory than they captured. In June, this trend became much clearer, with Russia's net territorial balance falling to approximately –40 km², indicating that Russian territorial losses substantially exceeded their gains. Ukrainian forces continued to conduct successful counterattacks on the Velyka Novosilka axis and, more importantly, north of Lyman, preventing Russian forces from establishing staging positions for attacks against Ukrainian GLOCs between Lyman and Slovyansk and thereby disrupting efforts to envelop the Slovyansk–Kramatorsk agglomeration from the north. The frontline remains highly porous. At present, we have identified more than 100 locations where Russian troops have been sighted ahead of their assessed FLOT. Presence does not necessarily equate to territorial control; however, unless these incursions are rapidly contained, Russian forces have repeatedly demonstrated an ability to consolidate their presence into firm territorial control and exploit weaknesses in Ukrainian defensive dispositions. Russian gains occurred in Sumy and Kharkiv Oblasts, near Kupyansk, along the Slovyansk–Kramatorsk–Kostiantynivka axis, and near Huliaipole. The Slovyansk–Kramatorsk–Kostiantynivka axis remains Russia's primary operational effort, with Russian personnel sighted approximately 12 km from Slovyansk. We assess that Russian forces are likely to continue achieving gradual, incremental advances in this area. (Data source for the monthly chat: Rochan and @Black_BirdGroup)

In #CaboVerde, irrigation is helping turn scarce water into stronger harvests, higher incomes and more resilient communities. On islands beyond the main tourism hubs, where agriculture remains a key source of employment, water scarcity has long constrained productivity, incomes and opportunity. Investments in irrigation infrastructure, solar-powered systems, local water governance and climate-smart agriculture are enabling rural communities to produce more, earn more and build more resilient local food systems. The results are clear: 🔹Crop production has increased by 77%. 🔹More than 518 hectares have been brought under cultivation. 🔹More than 21,000 people have directly benefited. Women and young people are gaining new skills, employment and leadership opportunities. This is what investing in the first mile of food systems looks like. Given how successfully the Ukrainians have been attacking Russian refineries, there’s no indication that they’ll stop attacking them. nitter.perennialte.ch/WarDroneXX/status/2073… WarDroneX (@WarDroneXX) Blyskava drone - The economics (3/5) ou can read the full article about the Blyskavka drone on my Substack - tymoteuszszaynok.substack.co… Ukraine's Blyskavka strike drone costs about $870. That single number explains most of the program. For comparison: a 155mm artillery shell runs several thousand dollars on Western production lines. A Western loitering munition with similar range and payload costs tens to hundreds of thousands. Ukrainian pilots use a simpler benchmark - the Blyskavka costs "two FPVs' worth of money" while carrying roughly four times the payload, several times farther. The price has barely moved as the drone improved: 35,000 hryvnias at launch in August 2025, about 38,500 (~$870) by mid-2026 - and that includes a +30% range upgrade introduced along the way. Cheapness changes how a weapon gets used. At under $900 per airframe, the Blyskavka can be expended against targets that would never justify a missile: one dugout, one howitzer, one enemy drone team. It can also be lost - to jamming, weather, ground fire - without the loss meaning much. A weapon affordable enough to risk freely gets flown constantly. A weapon flown constantly generates the combat feedback that drives the next round of upgrades. The economics and the iteration speed are the same story. The drone complements artillery rather than replacing it - guns deliver far more total explosive per day, in all weather, immune to jamming. The 80 km headline range requires a relay aircraft and a light warhead; heavily loaded missions fly much shorter. The baseline analogue video link is vulnerable to interference (fiber and digital variants fix that at extra cost). And a slow plywood aircraft can be intercepted - Ukraine hunts Russia's Molniya with cheap interceptors, and the same logic applies in reverse. But the category math is hard to argue with. The gap between FPV drones (cheap, short-ranged, small payload) and deep-strike systems (capable, scarce, expensive) is where targets at operational depth live. Both sides are racing to fill it, and the side that fills it at $870 per shot gets to take a lot of shots. Ukraine plans over 3 million FPV drones in 2026; the medium-range segment is scaling alongside. Cost per destroyed target, crews trained per month, components delivered per week - wars of attrition are decided by mundane arithmetic, and this aircraft is built around exactly that. OCI Cardholders, unable to download your e-OCI Card? Can't generate your e-OCI Card because your registered email address is no longer accessible? Update your email address on the OCI Portal to download your e-OCI card by following the next steps: 1. Visit the OCI Portal at ociservices.gov.in/ and register as a new user using your current email address 2. Log in, click Apply Online, and then select OCI Miscellaneous Services. 3. Access your OCI profile by entering: • Passport number last linked to your OCI Card • OCI Card number • Date of Birth 4. Select 'Email ID Updation' option, upload your OCI Card in PDF format and submit your application. 5. Once your application is approved, your OCI Card details will appear on the dashboard on the home page. Click on the e-OCI Card tab to generate and download your e-OCI Card. Acabo de conversar telefónicamente con el presidente de los EEUU Donald Trump. Cómo en las tres veces anteriores fue una conversación amable. Le solicite su ayuda para impedir que el odio creado en una parte de la sociedad colombiana no lleve a la sangre y la violencia de quienes los instigan y financian. Me dijo que era un " godman" y que ojalá pudiéramos hablar despues. Le advertí de la enorme polarización creciente entre la sociedad de los 5 países que libertó Simón Bolívar y que éstá hasta su muerte siempre llevo el mechón de pelo que le regaló George Washington. Le di todos los datos actuales del programa que adelanto de sustitución voluntaria de cultivos de hoja de Coca y que serán publicados par orgullo de mi gobierno y de la sociedad colombiana. Dejé financiado el programa hasta diciembre de este año 2026 y le solicité por su eficacia, que lo mantuvieran. Me extrañó que el presidente Donald Trump no supiera que yo no apoyaba a Abelardo de la Espriella y me sorprendió que no supiera que yo y mi familia aún estábamos incluidos en la lista OFAC, me prometió actuar en el tema.

Ambassador Mumin Chen and the delegation engaged in in-depth discussions on China–India relations, Taiwan–India relations, and future prospects for Taiwan–India cooperation. मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांच्या अध्यक्षतेखाली आज विधानभवन, मुंबई येथे पवना जलवाहिनी प्रकल्पाबाबत बैठक पार पडली. पिंपरी-चिंचवड शहराची भविष्यातील गरज लक्षात घेऊन राबविण्यात येणारा ‘पवना थेट समांतर जलवाहिनी प्रकल्प’ हा शेतकऱ्यांच्या संमतीने, विश्वासाने आणि संवादातूनच पुढे नेला जाईल. शेतकऱ्यांच्या भावना आणि मतांचा पूर्ण आदर राखून याबाबत निर्णय घेतले जातील. स्थानिक शेतकरी, स्थानिक सर्व लोकप्रतिनिधी, संबंधित शासनाचे विभाग यांची व्यापक चर्चा, परस्पर संवाद आणि विश्वासाच्या माध्यमातूनच या प्रश्नांवर कायमस्वरूपी तोडगा काढून हा प्रकल्प पुढे नेला जाईल, असे प्रतिपादन मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांनी यावेळी केले. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, राज्यात दिवसेंदिवस नवीन वसाहती वाढत आहेत, वाढत्या लोकसंख्येची गरज लक्षात घेऊन त्यानुसार पाण्याचे नियोजन आणि कार्यक्षम वापर झाला नाही, तर भविष्यात गंभीर जलसंकट निर्माण होऊ शकते. त्यामुळे पाण्याच्या प्रत्येक थेंबाचा योग्य वापर आणि दीर्घकालीन नियोजन करणे ही काळाची गरज आहे. पिंपरी-चिंचवड शहराची भविष्यातील गरज लक्षात घेऊन पवना थेट समांतर जलवाहिनी प्रकल्प हा शहरासाठी खूप महत्त्वाचा प्रकल्प ठरणार आहे. या प्रकल्पासाठी शेतकऱ्यांशी संवाद साधण्यासाठी शासन तयार आहे. स्थानिक लोकप्रतिनिधींनीदेखील यासाठी पुढाकार घ्यावा, शासनाकडून शेतकऱ्यांना दिलेली आश्वासने पूर्ण करावीत, यामध्ये दिरंगाई करू नये, असे निर्देश मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी दिले. कोणत्याही विकास प्रकल्पांना विरोध करण्याऐवजी लोकांचा विश्वास संपादन करून ते पुढे नेणे अधिक महत्त्वाचे आहे. यासाठी सर्व लोकप्रतिनिधी, सर्व राजकीय पक्ष, संबंधित विभाग आणि स्थानिक नागरिकांनी एकत्रितपणे काम करण्याची आवश्यकता आहे. महाराष्ट्राच्या विकासाचा वेग कायम ठेवत भविष्यातील गरजांचा विचार करून निर्णय घेणे आवश्यक आहे. विकासासोबतच शेतकऱ्यांच्या हिताचे संरक्षण करणे ही सरकारची सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकता आहे. गेल्या अनेक दशकांतील निर्णयांचा संपूर्ण भार आजच्या पिढीवर टाकून चालणार नाही. मजबूत पाया तयार केल्याशिवाय कोणताही विकास प्रकल्प यशस्वी होऊ शकत नाही, असे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले. पिंपरी-चिंचवडसह संपूर्ण पुणे महानगर प्रदेश लक्षात घेऊन 2050 पर्यंतचे दीर्घकालीन पाणी नियोजन करावे. वाढती लोकसंख्या, नागरीकरण आणि औद्योगिकीकरण लक्षात घेऊन भविष्यातील पिण्याच्या पाण्याची गरज, नवीन जलस्रोतांचे नियोजन आणि उपलब्ध जलस्रोतांचा कार्यक्षम वापर यासाठी समन्वित आराखडा तयार करावा. तसेच उपलब्ध पाण्याचा जास्तीत जास्त कार्यक्षम वापर करण्यासाठी सांडपाण्यावर प्रक्रिया करून त्याचा पुनर्वापर करण्यावर विशेष भर देण्याचे निर्देश मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी दिले. औद्योगिक, व्यावसायिक तसेच उद्याने, बांधकामे आणि इतर बिगर-पेयजल वापरासाठी प्रक्रिया केलेल्या पाण्याचा वापर वाढवून पिण्याच्या पाण्यावरील ताण कमी करण्यासाठी आवश्यक उपाययोजना तातडीने राबविण्याच्या सूचनाही मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी दिल्या. पवना थेट समांतर जलवाहिनी प्रकल्पामुळे पिंपरी-चिंचवडला शाश्वत, सुरक्षित आणि भविष्योन्मुख पाणीपुरवठा होणार पिंपरी-चिंचवड शहराच्या वाढत्या लोकसंख्येला शुद्ध, सुरक्षित आणि अखंड पाणीपुरवठा करण्याच्या उद्देशाने पवना धरण ते सेक्टर 23, निगडी जलशुद्धीकरण केंद्रादरम्यान पवना थेट समांतर जलवाहिनी प्रकल्प राबविण्यात येणार आहे. पवना धरणातील शुद्ध पाणी थेट जलशुद्धीकरण केंद्रापर्यंत प्रदूषणमुक्त आणि विश्वासार्ह पद्धतीने पोहोचविणे हे या प्रकल्पाचे प्रमुख उद्दिष्ट आहे. सध्या पिंपरी-चिंचवड शहराची लोकसंख्या सुमारे 38 लाख असून दररोज सुमारे 650 MLD पाणीपुरवठा केला जातो. यामध्ये पवना नदीतून 520 MLD, इंद्रायणी नदीतून 100 MLD आणि एमआयडीसीमार्फत 30 MLD पाणी मिळते. सध्याची पाण्याची मागणी सुमारे 655 MLD असून मंजूर पाणी आरक्षण 776 MLD आहे. लोकसंख्या वाढ लक्षात घेता हे आरक्षण 2029 पर्यंत पुरेसे राहणार असल्याचा अंदाज व्यक्त करण्यात आला आहे. प्रस्तावित अंदाजानुसार 2031 पर्यंत शहराची लोकसंख्या 55 लाखांवर पोहोचण्याची शक्यता असून पाण्याची मागणी 949 MLD होईल. 2041 मध्ये लोकसंख्या 95 लाखांवर गेल्यास मागणी 1638 MLD आणि 2051 मध्ये 135 लाख लोकसंख्येसाठी 2328 MLD पाण्याची आवश्यकता भासणार आहे. त्यामुळे भविष्यातील गरज लक्षात घेऊन हा प्रकल्प महत्त्वाचा ठरणार आहे. यावेळी विधानसभा उपाध्यक्ष अण्णा बनसोडे, मंत्री राधाकृष्ण विखे पाटील, खासदार श्रीरंग आप्पा बारणे, इतर आमदार व वरिष्ठ अधिकारी उपस्थित होते. @Dev_Fadnavis @anna_bansode_ @RVikhePatil @MPShrirangBarne #Maharashtra #DevendraFadnavis #PavanaProject

🚨🇫🇷🇩🇪 DÉFENSE EUROPÉENNE : LA FRANCE ÉCARTÉE D’EURODRONE Nouvel épisode des tensions franco-allemandes dans l’industrie de défense européenne. Selon plusieurs sources du secteur, Dassault Aviation aurait été écarté du programme Eurodrone, piloté par Airbus Defence & Space. Une décision qui relance une question fondamentale : L’Europe de la défense est-elle un projet de coopération… ou un instrument au service des intérêts nationaux les plus puissants ? ➡️ Pourquoi le principe du « meilleur industriel » est-il invoqué lorsqu’il sert certains acteurs, mais contesté lorsqu’il bénéficie à la France ? ➡️ Comment construire une autonomie stratégique européenne lorsque les grands programmes sont constamment paralysés par des rivalités nationales ? ➡️ La France finance-t-elle une Europe de la défense dont elle est progressivement exclue ? Le dossier Eurodrone illustre une réalité souvent passée sous silence. Derrière les discours sur la souveraineté européenne, les États continuent de défendre avant tout leurs propres intérêts industriels et technologiques. L’Allemagne réclame régulièrement un partage équilibré des responsabilités lorsque Paris est en position de force. Mais lorsque les rôles s’inversent, les règles semblent parfois changer. Le problème dépasse le seul cas Eurodrone. À force de blocages, de rivalités et de doubles standards, l’Europe risque de compromettre sa capacité à bâtir une véritable industrie de défense capable de rivaliser avec les États-Unis, la Chine ou la Russie. L’Europe de la défense ne pourra exister que si les règles sont les mêmes pour tous. Aujourd’hui, beaucoup commencent à en douter. The NITI TARA rollout continues to strengthen evidence-based governance across India. NITI TARA continues to advance NITI Aayog’s commitment to empowering States through data-driven governance and cooperative federalism. Building on the successful capacity-building sessions conducted last week, NITI Aayog organised two more NITI TARA (Toolkit for Analysis, Review & Action) training programmes in Kulgam, Jammu & Kashmir, and Dahod, Gujarat. Designed as an “Experience in a Box” solution, NITI TARA equips district and block administrations with integrated data, analytics, and visualisation tools to support evidence-based planning, real-time monitoring, and informed decision-making. The training programmes are strengthening the capacity of district and block administrations to translate data into actionable insights, enabling more targeted interventions and improved development outcomes across Aspirational Districts and Aspirational Blocks. As the rollout progresses, NITI TARA continues to enhance the ability of local administrations to leverage data for effective planning, monitoring, and implementation, further advancing evidence-based governance at the grassroots. Together, we are transforming evidence into action and strategy into measurable impact. #NITITara #CooperativeFederalism @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp

NITI Aayog convened a meeting under the chairpersonship of Dr. M. Srinivas, Member, NITI Aayog, to deliberate on the proposed Mentorship Framework for Students Belonging to Vulnerable Sections in Higher Education. The proposed framework envisions mentorship as a structured institutional support system to help students navigate socio-emotional, academic, and career-related challenges while promoting equitable access, holistic development, and improved learning outcomes across Higher Education Institutions. The meeting was attended by senior officials from NITI Aayog, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, the University Grants Commission, and leading academicians from IIM Lucknow, Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics, Banaras Hindu University, and Tata Institute of Social Sciences. By fostering meaningful mentorship and stronger institutional support, the initiative aims to create a more inclusive higher education ecosystem where every student has equitable access and opportunity to engage, learn, and succeed, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047. #HigherEducation #InclusiveEducation @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp

तकलादू पुरावे, 'चेन ऑफ इव्हेंट्स', साक्षीदार फितूर होणे या बाबींचा अभ्यास करून ही विशिष्ट कार्यपद्धती तयार करण्यात यावी. या कायद्याअंतर्गत तपास अधिकारी हा उपविभागीय पोलीस अधिकारी असतो. त्यामुळे राज्यभरात घेण्यात येणाऱ्या कार्यशाळांमध्ये प्रामुख्याने उपविभागीय पोलीस अधिकारी स्तरावरील प्रशिक्षण घेण्यात यावे. या कायद्याअंतर्गत दाखल खटल्यांच्या न्यायालयीन सुनावणीचे भारतीय न्याय संहितेतील तरतुदीनुसार व्हिडिओ चित्रीकरण करावे, जेणेकरून साक्षीदार फितूर होण्याचे प्रमाण कमी होईल, असे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, राज्यात सोलापूर, अहिल्यानगर, परभणी, नांदेड व यवतमाळ जिल्ह्यांमध्ये ॲट्रॉसिटी कायद्याअंतर्गत दाखल होणाऱ्या गुन्ह्यांचे प्रमाण जास्त असण्यामागील कारणे पोलीस यंत्रणेने शोधावीत. याबाबत अधिक सखोल चौकशी करून गुन्ह्यांचा अभ्यास करत अहवाल सादर करावा. कुठेही खोटे गुन्हे असल्यास, तपासाअंती ते दाखल करण्यात येऊ नयेत. या कायद्याअंतर्गत दाखल खटल्यांच्या सुनावणीदरम्यान खून, बलात्कार, दरोडे आदी गंभीर गुन्ह्यांतील साक्षीदारांचे संरक्षण करावे, त्यासाठी साक्षीदार संरक्षण कार्यक्रम राबविण्यात यावा. जिल्हास्तरावर कायद्याची प्रभावी अंमलबजावणी करत सरकारी वकिलांशी संवाद व समन्वय वाढविण्यात यावा. या कायद्याच्या अंमलबजावणीशी संबंधित सर्व यंत्रणांच्या कार्यशाळा घेऊन त्यांना प्रशिक्षित करावे. तसेच कायद्याच्या प्रभावी अंमलबजावणीसाठी राज्यस्तरावर मुख्यमंत्री यांच्या अध्यक्षतेखाली आणि पोलीस महासंचालक यांच्या अध्यक्षतेखाली वर्षातून सहा महिन्यांच्या अंतराने बैठक आयोजित करण्यात यावी, असे निर्देश मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी दिले. ॲट्रॉसिटी कायद्याअंतर्गत देण्यात आलेली आर्थिक मदत व हेल्पलाइनविषयी माहिती: ॲट्रॉसिटी कायद्यांतर्गत 2025-26 मध्ये 4524 पीडित व्यक्तींना आर्थिक #ICYMI: The #FBI is warning the public about an identity theft scheme wherein criminals impersonate the owners of vacant property parcels and attempt to illegally sell the property parcels without the owner’s knowledge or consent. The scam includes the following phases: Phase 1: Landowner Impersonation. Criminals create fake identifications (drivers licenses and/or U.S. passports), Outlook email addresses, and Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) generated phone numbers and use them to impersonate landowners. Criminals can obtain property parcel owner’s personally identifiable information through county or state public websites, data brokers, stolen account information, phishing schemes, or purchased from the dark web or hackers. Phase 2: Contact with Realtors and Title Companies. Criminals contact a local realtor and title company, pose as the property parcel owner, and draft property-related contracts to market and sell the vacant property parcels. In one instance, a fictious deed was used to further substantiate the impersonation and convince realtors of the validity of the sale. Phase 3: Payment. The criminals request the money from the illegal sale of the property be sent to a co-conspirator attorney in a different state. Learn more about this #scam and how to protect yourself at: ic3.gov/PSA/2026/PSA260616

Here is a short frontline summary for June 2026. Although we assessed that Russian forces gained approximately 25 km² in May 2026, we also noted that they may have lost more territory than they captured. In June, this trend became much clearer, with Russia's net territorial balance falling to approximately –40 km², indicating that Russian territorial losses substantially exceeded their gains. Ukrainian forces continued to conduct successful counterattacks on the Velyka Novosilka axis and, more importantly, north of Lyman, preventing Russian forces from establishing staging positions for attacks against Ukrainian GLOCs between Lyman and Slovyansk and thereby disrupting efforts to envelop the Slovyansk–Kramatorsk agglomeration from the north. The frontline remains highly porous. At present, we have identified more than 100 locations where Russian troops have been sighted ahead of their assessed FLOT. Presence does not necessarily equate to territorial control; however, unless these incursions are rapidly contained, Russian forces have repeatedly demonstrated an ability to consolidate their presence into firm territorial control and exploit weaknesses in Ukrainian defensive dispositions. Russian gains occurred in Sumy and Kharkiv Oblasts, near Kupyansk, along the Slovyansk–Kramatorsk–Kostiantynivka axis, and near Huliaipole. The Slovyansk–Kramatorsk–Kostiantynivka axis remains Russia's primary operational effort, with Russian personnel sighted approximately 12 km from Slovyansk. We assess that Russian forces are likely to continue achieving gradual, incremental advances in this area. (Data source for the monthly chat: Rochan and @Black_BirdGroup)

Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif offers prayers at the funeral of late Supreme Leader of Iran, Shaheed Ayatollah Sayyed Ali Khamenei. Tehran on 3 July 2026.

Tehran: 3 July 2026. At the invitation of the President of the Islamic Republic of Iran H.E Dr Masoud Pezeshkian, Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif attended the funeral ceremony of the late Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic of Iran, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, who had embraced martyrdom on 28th February, 2026 during the attacks on Iran. The Prime Minister led a high-level delegation from Pakistan that included Deputy Prime Minister & Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Chief of Army Staff & Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Interior Minister Syed Mohsin Naqvi, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Chairman Pakistan Peoples Party Bilawal Bhutto Zardari and other senior government officials. On this solemn occasion, the Prime Minister recalled the lasting contributions of the late Supreme Leader for Islam. He paid rich tribute to the late Supreme Leader, who guided the Iranian nation for decades, with remarkable wisdom and sagacity. The Prime Minister expressed full solidarity with Supreme Leader, His Eminence Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei, President Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian and the brotherly people of Iran in this moment of national grief and prayed to Allah Almighty for forgiveness of the departed leader. After attending the ceremony, the Prime Minister, who had arrived in Tehran earlier today, departed for Istanbul for his official visit to Turkiye. Parliamentary delegation led by Chairman Senate Syed Yousaf Raza Gillani and Speaker National Assembly Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, Parliamentarians and Chief Minister Sindh Syed Murad Ali Shah also attended the funeral along with the Prime Minister. 🇮🇳 🇨🇦 Christopher Skeete, Minister of International Relations and La Francophonie, Government of Québec, Canada, along with his delegation, met CM Devendra Fadnavis at Vidhan Bhavan in Mumbai, today. On the occasion, CM Devendra Fadnavis exchanged the Letter of Intent (LoI) between the Government of Maharashtra and the Le Govt du Québec, reaffirming its commitment to strengthening long-standing cooperation in technology, innovation, higher education, research and cultural exchange, while advancing sustainable growth and long-term collaboration. 1. The Iran-US ceasefire may be holding, but another conflict is quietly unfolding in West Asia. Not a hot war, but a cold one — between the US & its closest Arab ally, Saudi Arabia. #CutTheClutter explains what triggered the rift, why it is significant & what’s next for ties between the 2 countries. It also details how a new Middle East Security architecture is now taking shape. 2. The trigger was Trump’s ‘Project Freedom’. On May 3, he decided to launch an op. to escort merchant shipping vessels out of the Strait of Hormuz. But Saudi govt refused to allow the US to use its own bases in that country. This led to angry phone calls between Trump & the Saudi Crown Prince, reaching a point where US threatened to stop replenishment of interceptor missiles. 3. Eventually, things calmed down. But that relationship now seems quite fraught — MBS skipped the G7 Summit & Rubio, who travelled in the Gulf last week, skipped Saudi Arabia. There’s another complexity. Rulers of GCC countries are aligned with the US &, by implication, with Israel. But there’s public anger over Gaza & West Bank. So, there’s a fear their own people might turn on them if they continue to be complicit with US & Israel in fighting Iran. 4. So, what has Saudi Arabia done? It has made its own deals with Iran. The principle is that Iran is the neighbourhood bully, & it doesn’t have the ability or willingness to fight it. And, now the trusted patron appears inconsistent. The Saudis are trying a balancing act — while they might keep buying weapons from US & investing in Trump’s son-in-law’s company, they are also directly & indirectly paying protection money to Iran as well as Pakistan. 5. The fallout extends beyond Washington & Riyadh because within the GCC itself, the fault lines were already widening. Now, what will the Americans do? Indications are that now US will increasingly thin out its presence in Saudi Arabia & increase it in Bahrain, UAE, Israel & Jordan — countries that were more invested in the fight against Iran. 6. تہران: 3 جولائی 2026. وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف کا دورہءِ ایران، وزیرِ اعظم کی ایران کے مرحوم سپریم لیڈر آیت اللہ سید علی خامنہ ای شہید کی آخری رسومات میں شرکت. وزیرِ اعظم محمد شہباز شریف اعلی سطح وفد کے ہمراہ اپنے ایک روزہ دورہءِ ایران کیلئے تہران پہنچ گئے ہیں. مہرآباد ایئرپورٹ پر ایران کے وزیرِ داخلہ، جناب اسکندر مومنی تہران میں پاکستان کے سفیر، عزت مآب عمران احمد صدیقی اور پاکستان و ایران کے اعلی سفارتی حکام نے وزیراعظم کا استقبال کیا۔ وزیراعظم شہباز شریف تہران میں ایران کے مرحوم سپریم لیڈر، آیت اللہ سید علی خامنہ ای شہید کی آخری رسومات میں شرکت کریں گے۔ وزیراعظم پاکستانی عوام اور حکومت کی جانب سے ایرانی قیادت اور سوگوار خاندانوں سے دلی تعزیت کا اظہار کریں گے اور غم کی اس گھڑی میں برادر ایرانی قوم کے ساتھ پاکستان کی مکمل یکجہتی کا اعادہ کریں گے۔ اسپیکر نیشنل اسمبلی سردار ایاز صادق، نائب وزیراعظم و وزیر خارجہ سینیٹر محمد اسحاق ڈار، چیف آف آرمی اسٹاف و چیف آف ڈیفینس فورسز فیلڈ مارشل سید عاصم منیر، وزیرِ اطلاعات و نشریات عطاء اللہ تارڑ، چیئرمین پاکستان پیپلز پارٹی بلاول بھٹو زرداری، نئیر بخاری، وزیرِ اعلی سندھ سید مراد علی شاہ اور پارلیمینٹیرئینز وزیرِ اعظم کے ہمراہ آخری رسومات میں شرکت کریں گے. اسلام آباد : 3 جولائی، 2026. وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف کی زیر صدارت ایڈز اور ہیپاٹائٹس سی جیسے متعدی امراض کی روک تھام کے لیے اٹھائے گئے اقدامات پر جائزہ اجلاس آج اسلام آباد میں منعقد ہوا. اجلاس میں وزیرِ اعظم نے ہدایت کی کہ متعدی امراض کے پھیلاؤ کے فوری سد باب کے لیے ملک بھر میں غیر معیاری سرنجز کی تیاری اور استعمال پر مکمل پابندی لگائی جائے. خلاف ضابطہ سرنجز کے استعمال میں ملوث یا اسکی روک تھام میں مجرمانہ غفلت کے مرتکب افراد اور ہسپتالوں کے خلاف قانونی کارروائی کی جائے. وزیراعظم نے متعدی امراض پر قابو پانے کیلئے ماہرین کی خصوصی کمیٹی تشکیل دینے کی ہدایت کی. گفتگو کرتے ہوئے وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ کمیٹی اپنی سفارشات مرتب کرتے وقت صوبوں سے مشاورت یقینی بنائے. وزرات قانون متعلقہ اداروں کے ساتھ مل کر قانونی اور ریگولیٹری فریم ورک میں ضروری ترامیم تجویز کرے. قومی سطح پر جامع حکمت عملی کی تشکیل اور موثر نفاذ ہی اس مسئلے کا حل ہے. سرنجز سے متعدی امراض کے پھیلنے کے مستقل سدباب کیلئے ڈریپ (DRAP) میڈیکل آلات کی انڈسٹری سے مشاورت کرکے پالیسی اقدامات تجویز کرے. وزیرِ اعظم نے مزید کہا کہ متعدی امراض کے پھیلاؤ کے سد باب کی جاری کوششوں میں بین الاقوامی شراکت داروں کی معاونت انتہائی اہم ہے. علاج سے متعلقہ آلات کی مینوفیکچرنگ اور شعبہ صحت کے عملہ کی عالمی معیار کی ٹریننگ پر بھی خصوصی توجہ دینے کی ضرورت ہے۔ اجلاس میں وزیراعظم کی ہدایت پر قائم کردہ خصوصی ٹاسک فورس اور وزرات قومی صحت کی جانب سے متعدی امراض کے پھیلاؤ کے سد باب کے لیے اٹھاۓ گئے اقدامات پر بریفنگ دی گئی۔ اجلاس میں وفاقی وزیر قانون اعظم نذیر تارڑ، وزیر مملکت برائے صحت ڈاکٹر مختار احمد بھرت، اٹارنی جنرل آف پاکستان منصور اعوان ، گلوبل فنڈ کی نمائندہ Izaskun Gaviria، پبلک ہیلتھ کے ماہرین، وزرات قومی صحت، ڈریپ کے نمائندگان اور اعلی سرکاری حکام نے شرکت کی۔ Video

India's most creditworthy borrowers are also its most underfinanced entrepreneurs Women are more reliable borrowers than men. Their loan delinquency rate is 2.8%, compared with 3.3% for men, and they default less often than the overall market (as per data from CRIF High Mark). Therefore, by standard risk measures, they are the safer segment. However, the disparity emerges in the size of credit extended rather than in access to it. Women now hold close to half of all business-loan accounts but receive only 28% of the total value disbursed. In other words, women are borrowing in large numbers, but in consistently smaller amounts. The constraint is no longer obtaining credit; it is obtaining credit sufficient to grow. This gap widens at the point where enterprises begin to scale. Only about 4% of women-owned businesses use cash-credit or overdraft facilities, the revolving working-capital lines expanding firms rely on, against nearly 40% economy-wide (TransUnion CIBIL, NITI Aayog and MicroSave Consulting's report "From Borrowers to Builders, 2026"). Without them, many women entrepreneurs stay locked into micro-enterprise, unable to make the jump to larger operations. Smaller loans limit expansion. Limited expansion reduces both the need and the eligibility for larger credit. The cycle feeds itself: businesses stay small not because they're riskier, but because they're financed as though they won't grow. The policy question is shifting, from access to a first loan, to enabling women to qualify for larger, subsequent rounds. When the lowest-risk borrowers get the smallest amounts of capital, that's not sound lending. That's a persistent gap in the credit market.

🇦🇫 | Des délégués des talibans et de la Résistance du Nord en Afghanistan ont assisté aux funérailles malgré le fait qu’ils soient en guerre. 📝 La présence conjointe de représentants talibans et du NRF aux funérailles de Khamenei confirme la stratégie iranienne du “double canal” en Afghanistan : soutien discret et logistique au NRF comme levier de réserve, tout en consolidant une relation diplomatique et économique croissante avec les talibans sans jamais les reconnaître officiellement. Cette ambiguïté stratégique calculée permet à Téhéran de rester incontournable quel que soit le futur équilibre de pouvoir à Kaboul, en accueillant sur son sol des ennemis jurés sans que ni l’un ni l’autre n’ait intérêt à rompre publiquement l’unité de façade voulue pour l’occasion. Pour le NRF, l’enjeu est purement symbolique : exister diplomatiquement à défaut de peser militairement, en s’affichant dans un espace où il croise un rival qui contrôle pourtant le pays. Pour les talibans, c’est une occasion de plus de consolider leur reconnaissance régionale via un partenaire pragmatique, malgré des tensions persistantes sur les frontières et l’eau. Le point de fragilité reste que Massoud a lui-même publiquement mis en cause la sécurité offerte par l’Iran aux Afghans anti-talibans après l’assassinat du général Sari à Téhéran, donc cette coexistence protocolaire ne traduit ni confiance ni alliance stable, mais un calcul tactique de circonstance des deux côtés.

🇰🇷🤖 | Le géant industriel sud-coréen Hyundai prévoit d'installer 25 000 robots humanoïdes dans ses usines, ignorant l'opposition totale des syndicats de travailleurs. Le projet de Hyundai illustre parfaitement la destruction créatrice de Schumpeter : l’innovation (les robots humanoïdes) remplace progressivement certains emplois industriels traditionnels, mais crée en parallèle de nouveaux métiers dans la robotique, l’IA, la maintenance et l’ingénierie. À court terme, cette transition suscite des craintes légitimes pour l’emploi, tandis qu’à long terme, elle vise à accroître la productivité, la compétitivité et à faire émerger une nouvelle structure économique fondée sur des activités à plus forte valeur ajoutée.

80 years after the opening of the International Military Tribunal for the Far East, or Tokyo Trials, a comprehensive Chinese translation of its records has been published for the first time, offering new access to one of the 20th century's most consequential judicial proceedings. The project fills a longstanding gap in Chinese-language documentation in the area. Their translation into Chinese, scholars noted, opens new avenues for research while broadening public understanding of the trial's historical significance. From May 3, 1946, to Nov. 12, 1948, the International Military Tribunal for the Far East was held in Tokyo by 11 countries, including the United States, China, the UK and the Soviet Union, to try Japan's Class-A war criminals after World War II. During the trial some 80 years ago, the tribunal convicted 25 Class-A Japanese war criminals, with seven sentenced to death, including Hideki Tojo, the most atrocious war criminal who served as Japanese prime minister between 1941 and 1944. The proceedings, backed by extensive evidence, exposed the crimes of Japanese militarism and stood as a landmark victory of justice over aggression. More: xhtxs.cn/bdl8

Even as vehicles continued to pass through the toll barriers in both directions, flames suddenly erupted, engulfing the tanker and nearby toll booths within moments. The tanker driver, Dharmendra Dubey (40), and toll employee Alok Singh (26) died on the day of the accident. En ese marco, la justicia imputó a seis efectivos de la Policía de Córdoba por los delitos de privación ilegítima de la libertad y homicidio culposo en el marco de la investigación por su muerte. La muerte de Tomás Orihuela desató una fuerte reacción social en el barrio Bajo Pueyrredón, donde se sucedieron protestas y enfrentamientos entre vecinos y fuerzas de seguridad. স্বাধীনতা পরবর্তী সময়ে পার্বত্য চট্টগ্রামে বীর সেনানিদের বীরত্বগাঁথা আজ শহীদ নায়েক আফাজ উদ্দিন, বীর বিক্রম, ইস্ট বেঙ্গল-এর ৪৮তম শাহাদাত বার্ষিকী শহীদ নায়েক আফাজ উদ্দিন, বীর বিক্রম, ১৯৭৮ সালে ২০ ইস্ট বেঙ্গল এর সাথে পানছড়ি জোনে কর্মরত ছিলেন। গত ৩ জুলাই ১৯৭৮ তারিখে পানছড়ি এলাকায় একটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ অপারেশনে অংশগ্রহণ করেন। গোয়েন্দা তথ্যের ভিত্তিতে, ২০ ইস্ট বেঙ্গল থেকে একজন অফিসার, একজন জেসিও এবং ৩৯ জন অন্যান্য পদবীর সেনাসদস্য নিয়ে একটি টহল পাঠানো হয়। টহল দলটি লেফটেন্যান্ট মুস্তাফা হেলালের নেতৃত্বে তিনটি সেকশনে বিভক্ত ছিল, যেখানে নায়েক আফাজ উদ্দিন ছিলেন ৩ নম্বর সেকশনের সেকশন কমান্ডার। ভোর ৪:৩০ ঘটিকায় দলটি নির্ধারিত স্থানে পৌঁছায় এবং দুটি দলে বিভক্ত হয়। নায়েক আফাজ উদ্দিন অত্যন্ত সাহসিকতার সাথে শত্রুর অবস্থানকৃত কুঁড়েঘরের কাছে এগিয়ে যান। শত্রু পালানোর চেষ্টা করলে তিনি তাদের প্রতিহত করেন এবং সাহসের সাথে একজন শত্রুকে ধরে ফেলেন। শত্রুরা পালিয়ে যাওয়ার সময় একটি গ্রেনেড ছুঁড়ে দেয়, যার স্পিন্টারে নায়েক আফাজ উদ্দিন আহত হন। তীব্র আঘাত সত্ত্বেও, তিনি তাঁর এসএমজি দিয়ে পালিয়ে যাওয়া শত্রুদের উপর গুলি চালান এবং তাদের তাড়া করেন। তার ডান বুকের নীচে প্রচুর রক্তক্ষরণ হচ্ছিল, তবুও তিনি অপারেশন চালিয়ে যান। নায়েক আফাজ উদ্দিনকে দ্রুত পানছড়ি ক্যাম্পে স্থানান্তর করা হলেও তিনি একইদিন ভোর ৬:৪৫ মিনিটে মৃত্যুবরণ করেন। তাঁর সাহসিকতা, দায়িত্ববোধ ও আত্মত্যাগের জন্য তিনি মহামান্য রাষ্ট্রপতি কর্তৃক "বীর বিক্রম" খেতাবে ভূষিত হন।

An active-duty U.S. Air Force major who was arrested by U.S. Capitol Police yesterday after conducting a protest on the Capitol steps while in uniform calling for the impeachment of President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance is now under investigation by the Pentagon. Service members are prohibited from participating in partisan political activities while in uniform and are subject to additional restrictions under the Uniform Code of Military Justice regarding public statements about senior government officials. Without identifying the officer, the office of Air Force Secretary Troy Meink acknowledged reports of the incident, stating that an investigation "will proceed unimpeded." The Department of the Air Force also reiterated that all personnel are expected to comply with laws, regulations, and policies governing conduct and the wear of the uniform.

The U.S. Coast Guard has released additional details on the June 22 MH-60T "Jayhawk" helicopter crash on Harbor Mountain near Sitka, Alaska. All four crew members sustained only minor injuries and were released from the local hospital the same day. While the cause of the crash remains under investigation, a newly released photo from U.S. Coast Guard District Arctic shows the aircraft sustained extensive damage. Beginning next week, the Alaska Army National Guard's Downed Aircraft Recovery Team will begin recovery operations at the crash site, which remains closed to the public due to hazardous conditions. In the meantime, Coast Guard Air Station Kodiak continues supporting search & rescue coverage while Air Station Sitka works toward resuming flight operations next week. Source: news.uscg.mil/Press-Releases…

Le solicito a los medios públicos la transmisión de las reuniones de empalme de gobierno Voces (@vocesco) #Voces | El presidente Gustavo Petro propuso que el proceso de empalme entre su gobierno y la administración entrante de Abelardo de la Espriella sea transmitido por televisión, con el objetivo de que los colombianos puedan conocer de primera mano cómo avanza la entrega del Estado y el intercambio de información entre ambos equipos. La propuesta fue planteada en medio de las tensiones que han rodeado el inicio de la transición presidencial. Según el mandatario, la transmisión permitiría garantizar mayor transparencia y evitar especulaciones sobre el contenido de las reuniones, los informes de las entidades y las decisiones adoptadas durante el proceso de empalme. El planteamiento surge luego de que el equipo del presidente electo denunciara presuntas irregularidades en los últimos días de la administración Petro, entre ellas nombramientos y decisiones administrativas que, según la nueva administración, deberían ser revisadas durante el empalme. Por su parte, el Gobierno ha reiterado que entregará toda la información conforme a los procedimientos establecidos por la ley. De acuerdo con el cronograma definido para la transición, el proceso contempla la instalación de mesas sectoriales en las diferentes entidades del Estado, la socialización de informes de gestión y la elaboración de las actas finales que deberán entregarse antes de la posesión del nuevo gobierno. Incluso, el protocolo prevé una reunión entre el presidente saliente y el presidente electo, aunque hasta el momento no se ha confirmado una fecha para ese encuentro. La iniciativa de televisar el empalme aún no ha sido aceptada oficialmente por el equipo de Abelardo de la Espriella. Sin embargo, la propuesta se suma a las discusiones sobre cómo garantizar una transición transparente en medio de un ambiente político marcado por la polarización y los cuestionamientos entre el Gobierno saliente y la administración entrante. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/vocesco/status/2072789949921833396#m

Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, and Prof. K. V. Raju, Member, NITI Aayog, participated in a panel discussion on "Data, Statistics and India's Growth Agenda", held as part of "Swarna Andhra @ 2047: Economic Intelligence for Governance", a two-day capacity-building programme organised by the Planning Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh. The panel was moderated by Shri Suresh Goyal, Director General, NCAER, and featured Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI; Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Adviser, Government of India; and Prof. S. Mahendra Dev, Chairman, EAC-PM, as fellow panellists. Dr. Balasubramaniam emphasised that data must serve as a foundation for dignity in governance, making visible those often overlooked in averages, including informal workers and tribal communities. He noted that while India already has rich individual-level data, the priority now is to harmonise datasets across ministries, break institutional silos, and use evidence to strengthen social development and citizen capability. As India advances towards Viksit Bharat, he stressed that better decisions depend on engaging with what the data truly reveals and viewing citizens as active participants in the development journey. The programme's broader context was set by Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu, whose address emphasised translating the State's growth vision into measurable, mission-mode outcomes, integrating datasets across departments and geographies, and pursuing growth that is sustainable and inclusive. @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp @drrbalu

When it comes to protecting the lives and livelihoods of our people, there is no Government or Opposition only Sri Lanka. Today, at the National Council for Disaster Management chaired by H.E the President, I shared a strategic science-backed proposal to help Sri Lanka prepare for the anticipated climate risks of 2026–27. My message was simple; we cannot afford to wait for disaster to strike we must act. By strengthening early warning systems, safeguarding our food and water security, and planning together as a nation, we can create greater resilience against climate change. NewsWire 🇱🇰 (@NewsWireLK) Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has proposed a series of measures to strengthen Sri Lanka’s climate resilience and disaster preparedness, warning that the country should act now to prepare for the anticipated impacts of the 2026-2027 El Niño cycle. Speaking at the National Council for Disaster Management, chaired by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, Premadasa said climate security has become a national priority that requires a united, science-based response beyond political differences. Citing global scientific assessments, Premadasa warned that the developing El Niño could be among the strongest in recent decades, bringing prolonged droughts followed by severe flooding. He said Sri Lanka should move away from responding to disasters after they occur and instead adopt an anticipatory governance model based on scientific forecasting, risk assessments and early preparedness. Among his key proposals was making climate resilience a whole-of-government responsibility involving institutions responsible for agriculture, water resources, energy, health, finance, defence, provincial administration and local government. Premadasa also called for integrated reservoir management to improve water security, expansion of climate-smart agriculture to strengthen food security, and the modernisation of early warning systems through impact-based forecasting that provides communities with more actionable information before disasters strike. He further proposed strengthening disaster risk financing, improving preparedness for heatwaves and public health emergencies, enhancing the resilience of critical infrastructure, and establishing a National Climate Risk and Disaster Intelligence Centre to support evidence-based decision-making across Government. Premadasa said Sri Lanka should also draw lessons from countries such as India and Australia, which have strengthened climate forecasting, agricultural contingency planning and broader resilience initiatives in response to growing climate risks. Looking beyond the immediate El Niño threat, he proposed the preparation of a Presidential White Paper on National Climate Resilience and Disaster Preparedness to establish a long-term policy framework that would guide future governments. He stressed that climate resilience cannot be achieved by the Government alone and requires the participation of Parliament, provincial and local authorities, the scientific community, universities, the private sector, civil society, international development partners and local communities. Premadasa added that protecting the lives and livelihoods of Sri Lankans must remain a shared national responsibility. Dr Nika Soon-Shiong said she was removed from the board of the Committee to Protect Journalists after challenging a decision she feared would see Palestinians broadly excluded from journalist death tolls. She told MEE “there are bad faith attacks” on the organisation seeking to lobby against Palestinians’ inclusion. Last week, the CPJ said it was reviewing its documentation of journalists killed during the Israel-Gaza War. 20 Palestinians were delisted after militant groups published obituaries identifying them as members. International law protects the civilian status of journalists working for state or militant groups on the condition they are not directly involved in combat. The CPJ’s board has since voted against changes to their definition of journalist, in a move welcomed by Soon-Shiong. The press freedom group rejected claims it had sought to exclude particular groups, and flatly denied that political influence played a role in triggering the review. Video

One week after the devastating earthquakes in Venezuela, which have claimed close to 2,000 lives and left many more dead, injured, displaced, or still unaccounted for, we mourn with the families and communities affected by this tragedy. As humanitarian needs continue to grow, it is essential that assistance reaches all those in need in a timely, transparent, and non-discriminatory manner. Venezuelan authorities should facilitate, rather than hinder, the delivery of aid and access to affected communities. Independent civil society organizations can play a vital role in monitoring relief efforts, identifying gaps in assistance, and helping ensure accountability. They should be granted access to transparent information and data necessary to assess needs, monitor the response, and verify official statistics. Authorities should also provide information on the whereabouts and conditions of all political prisoners and immediately release those arbitrarily detained. At this critical moment, transparency, accountability, and respect for humanitarian principles are indispensable to an effective response and to protecting the rights of all those affected. LabPazVe (@LabPazVe) Laboratorio de Paz. A 1 semana de los terremotos del 24.06.2026. Los terremotos ocurridos el 24 de junio de 2026 han dejado una profunda huella de dolor, pérdidas humanas, personas heridas, familias damnificadas, viviendas destruidas o severamente afectadas, comunidades enteras en situación de vulnerabilidad y una enorme incertidumbre para millones de personas dentro y fuera del país. A una semana del trágico evento, el Laboratorio de Paz reafirma su profundo respeto y solidaridad con las víctimas fatales, sus familiares, las personas heridas, quienes han perdido sus hogares, sus pertenencias, sus medios de vida, y con todas las comunidades afectadas en el país. Acompañamos el dolor de quienes hoy aún esperan noticias de sus seres queridos y reconocemos la angustia de miles de familias que permanecen fuera de sus viviendas esperando noticias de sus familiares. A pesar del tiempo transcurrido desde los sismos, es indispensable que las labores de búsqueda, rescate y recuperación continúen con todos los recursos disponibles. Mientras exista la posibilidad de encontrar personas con vida, no podemos perder la esperanza. Cada minuto cuenta, cada esfuerzo importa y cada vida debe ser buscada con la máxima diligencia, coordinación y humanidad. La magnitud de esta tragedia exige que se mantenga el despliegue de equipos especializados, asistencia internacional, apoyo técnico y presencia humanitaria en las zonas más afectadas. Nuevamente insistimos en la obligación de primacía de la dignidad para atender la crisis, claridad, transparencia y responsabilidad en el manejo de la información sobre personas fallecidas, heridas, desaparecidas, rescatadas y damnificadas. Las familias tienen derecho a saber. El país tiene derecho a información pública, verificable, oportuna y desagregada. La opacidad y limitaciones al derecho a la información no protege a nadie; aumenta la angustia, dificulta la asistencia, obstaculiza la identificación de necesidades y debilita aún más la confianza en la respuesta. La atención a quienes lo perdieron todo debe ser eficaz, rápida, digna y sin discriminación. Las personas damnificadas necesitan refugios seguros, agua, alimentos, atención médica, apoyo psicosocial, información clara, protección frente a abusos, soluciones habitacionales sostenibles rápidas. La emergencia debe ser atendida con enfoque de derechos humanos, transparencia en el uso de los recursos y participación de la sociedad y de las comunidades afectadas. No pueden repetirse experiencias pasadas, respuestas improvisadas o asistencias temporales sin seguimiento. Esta emergencia debe ser asumida con memoria, responsabilidad y aprendizaje. La reconstrucción no puede convertirse en una nueva fuente de exclusión, abandono, corrupción o revictimización. Destacamos la labor fundamental de periodistas, comunicadores y trabajadores de la prensa que han estado cubriendo la emergencia desde el primer momento, muchas veces en condiciones precarias, con recursos propios y bajo restricciones. Su trabajo es indispensable para documentar lo ocurrido, orientar a la ciudadanía, visibilizar necesidades, verificar información, acompañar a las víctimas y exigir respuestas Reconocemos con profundo orgullo la fortaleza, la capacidad solidaria y la dignidad del pueblo venezolano. En medio del dolor, millones de personas han salido de forma independiente, autónoma y libre a ayudar a vecinos, a remover escombros, a crear centros de acopio, atender la salud sin descanso, a informar sin sesgos, a arriesgar su vida por rescatar a otros, a compartir lo poco de un país en emergencia humanitaria estancada. Aun teniendo poco, hemos dado con el corazón abierto. Esa solidaridad expresa lo mejor del país y demuestra que Venezuela cuenta con una reserva moral inmensa para enfrentar esta tragedia. Hoy Venezuela es solidaridad, dignidad y humanidad. Frente a las tragedias, nunca nos hemos resignarnos ni acostumbrarnos al dolor. Venceremos esta dura prueba, somos venezolanos y venezolanas. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/LabPazVe/status/2072447670833315971#m

Among the targets was an ambulance station, where three paramedics and three driver-technicians were injured. The city’s healthcare system was overwhelmed, with reports that 110 ambulance crews were working simultaneously to respond to emergencies. “We start a new day yet again with shock and horror - the idea that ambulance and emergency-response teams have to dig people out from the remains of destroyed residential blocks – and save the lives of their own colleagues who have been targeted,” says Robin Meldrum, Country Director for MSF in Ukraine. We once again emphasise that medical workers and healthcare facilities throughout Ukraine remain unprotected, working under constant threat and on the verge of resource depletion. We condemn the attacks by Russian forces, which endanger not only people but also their ability to receive medical care after being wounded.

My meeting with 🇹🇷 Health Minister Prof Dr Kemal Memişoğlu was above all an opportunity to say thank you: for Türkiye’s leadership, hospitality and partnership throughout the WHO Ministerial Conference on advancing health security through earthquake emergency management. Together, our teams at Türkiye’s Ministry of Health and WHO/Europe turned months of preparation into a tangible result: the Istanbul Outcome Statement on protecting health in earthquakes. For me, these 2 days showed the WHO I believe in: convening countries, learning from real experience, and helping shape shared standards and norms for stronger earthquake emergency management. I thanked Türkiye for making health a dedicated part of the #COP31 agenda in Antalya and reaffirmed WHO/Europe’s readiness to support cooperation on climate and health. We also discussed our partnership on Anatolian medicine and how Türkiye’s experience can be shared more widely, with a focus on evidence, safety, quality and people-centred care.

Preparations for the 50th anniversary of the Alma-Ata Declaration on Primary Health Care were a key focus of my exchange with Dr Akmaral Alnazarova, Kazakhstan’s Minister of Health. Meeting on the margins of the WHO Ministerial Conference in Istanbul on advancing health security through earthquake emergency management, we also explored how the Istanbul Outcome Statement can support practical cooperation through the network of Emergency Medical Teams under the Organization of Turkic States. I welcomed Kazakhstan’s interest in WHO classification of Emergency Medical Teams, and discussed the value of a Joint External Evaluation to assess capacities to prevent, detect and respond to public health threats, and to guide future investments in health security.

VIDEO | Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri (@HardeepSPuri) addresses concerns over ethanol-blended fuel. Addressing a press conference in Delhi, he says, "Somebody is saying that fuel mileage is going to drop. It is now well established that ethanol is even used in racing cars. Acceleration improves. What is that called? Knocking? Knocking also improves. Mileage? Yes, it may drop a little. But it may drop slightly due to various factors... Secondly, after consulting all stakeholders, including SIAM and ARAI, we have reached this stage. Then someone says, 'Your insurance will no longer cover this'. Insurance companies have already clarified that there is no such issue. But who benefits from spreading this false narrative? I am not going to make any accusations, but one thing should be very clear. There is enough space in India's growing consumer market for all technologies to coexist. There is room for electric vehicles, biofuel blended vehicles, and we are currently only at 20 per cent ethanol blending. If we move from 20 per cent to 25 per cent, it will happen only after all the necessary tests have been completed. There is also enough space for hybrid vehicles and CNG vehicles..." Independent civil society organizations can play a vital role in monitoring relief efforts, identifying gaps in assistance, and helping ensure accountability. They should be granted access to transparent information and data necessary to assess needs, monitor the response, and verify official statistics. Authorities should also provide information on the whereabouts and conditions of all political prisoners and immediately release those arbitrarily detained. At this critical moment, transparency, accountability, and respect for humanitarian principles are indispensable to an effective response and to protecting the rights of all those affected. LabPazVe (@LabPazVe) Laboratorio de Paz. A 1 semana de los terremotos del 24.06.2026. Los terremotos ocurridos el 24 de junio de 2026 han dejado una profunda huella de dolor, pérdidas humanas, personas heridas, familias damnificadas, viviendas destruidas o severamente afectadas, comunidades enteras en situación de vulnerabilidad y una enorme incertidumbre para millones de personas dentro y fuera del país. A una semana del trágico evento, el Laboratorio de Paz reafirma su profundo respeto y solidaridad con las víctimas fatales, sus familiares, las personas heridas, quienes han perdido sus hogares, sus pertenencias, sus medios de vida, y con todas las comunidades afectadas en el país. Acompañamos el dolor de quienes hoy aún esperan noticias de sus seres queridos y reconocemos la angustia de miles de familias que permanecen fuera de sus viviendas esperando noticias de sus familiares. A pesar del tiempo transcurrido desde los sismos, es indispensable que las labores de búsqueda, rescate y recuperación continúen con todos los recursos disponibles. Mientras exista la posibilidad de encontrar personas con vida, no podemos perder la esperanza. Cada minuto cuenta, cada esfuerzo importa y cada vida debe ser buscada con la máxima diligencia, coordinación y humanidad. La magnitud de esta tragedia exige que se mantenga el despliegue de equipos especializados, asistencia internacional, apoyo técnico y presencia humanitaria en las zonas más afectadas. Nuevamente insistimos en la obligación de primacía de la dignidad para atender la crisis, claridad, transparencia y responsabilidad en el manejo de la información sobre personas fallecidas, heridas, desaparecidas, rescatadas y damnificadas. Las familias tienen derecho a saber. El país tiene derecho a información pública, verificable, oportuna y desagregada. La opacidad y limitaciones al derecho a la información no protege a nadie; aumenta la angustia, dificulta la asistencia, obstaculiza la identificación de necesidades y debilita aún más la confianza en la respuesta. La atención a quienes lo perdieron todo debe ser eficaz, rápida, digna y sin discriminación. Las personas damnificadas necesitan refugios seguros, agua, alimentos, atención médica, apoyo psicosocial, información clara, protección frente a abusos, soluciones habitacionales sostenibles rápidas. La emergencia debe ser atendida con enfoque de derechos humanos, transparencia en el uso de los recursos y participación de la sociedad y de las comunidades afectadas. No pueden repetirse experiencias pasadas, respuestas improvisadas o asistencias temporales sin seguimiento. Esta emergencia debe ser asumida con memoria, responsabilidad y aprendizaje. La reconstrucción no puede convertirse en una nueva fuente de exclusión, abandono, corrupción o revictimización. Destacamos la labor fundamental de periodistas, comunicadores y trabajadores de la prensa que han estado cubriendo la emergencia desde el primer momento, muchas veces en condiciones precarias, con recursos propios y bajo restricciones. Su trabajo es indispensable para documentar lo ocurrido, orientar a la ciudadanía, visibilizar necesidades, verificar información, acompañar a las víctimas y exigir respuestas Reconocemos con profundo orgullo la fortaleza, la capacidad solidaria y la dignidad del pueblo venezolano. En medio del dolor, millones de personas han salido de forma independiente, autónoma y libre a ayudar a vecinos, a remover escombros, a crear centros de acopio, atender la salud sin descanso, a informar sin sesgos, a arriesgar su vida por rescatar a otros, a compartir lo poco de un país en emergencia humanitaria estancada. Aun teniendo poco, hemos dado con el corazón abierto. Esa solidaridad expresa lo mejor del país y demuestra que Venezuela cuenta con una reserva moral inmensa para enfrentar esta tragedia. Hoy Venezuela es solidaridad, dignidad y humanidad. Frente a las tragedias, nunca nos hemos resignarnos ni acostumbrarnos al dolor. Venceremos esta dura prueba, somos venezolanos y venezolanas. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/LabPazVe/status/2072447670833315971#m

The Delhi Government has notified a comprehensive Winter Pollution Master Plan to tackle seasonal air pollution through timely, preventive and technology-driven measures. Key measures effective from 1 November to 28 February include: 🔹Strict enforcement of ‘No PUC, No Fuel’ 🔹Restriction on the entry of non-BS VI vehicles from outside Delhi 🔹Work From Home for up to 50% of employees, whenever required 🔹Higher parking charges to encourage greater use of public transport 🔹Mandatory Anti-Smog/Mist Systems at large construction sites, along with stricter controls on construction activities 🔹A complete ban on burning waste, leaves and biomass 🔹Drone-based monitoring and strict enforcement against violations The Master Plan reflects the Delhi Government’s commitment to ensuring cleaner air and a healthier winter for every citizen. #ViksitDelhi

Meanwhile, Ukraine’s own military of defense has been publishing the opposite trend when it comes to Russia. Why? Fourth, the energy war. Why has this year seen Ukraine put pressure on Russian energy? What about vice versa? And does it even matter? Fifth, the front. Though obfuscated in the media, the battlefield is still moving, and largely in one direction. Sixth, drones. While quantitative production levels matter, what is far more important is the effectiveness of the units wielding them. And just how many of these effective units there are. This year has seen quite interesting developments on this front for both armies. This is what will really determine the future. As well the seventh trend, that of Starlink, and its emerging Russian analogue. It is intelligence and connectivity, more than anything else, which is the most powerful weapon wielded by Washington. AMK Mapping 🇳🇿 (@AMK_Mapping_) Preliminary figures for last night's combined missile and drone attack on Ukraine: ~30 Kh-101 cruise missiles launched, ~10 intercepted. ~24 Iskander-M ballistic missiles launched, ~6 intercepted. ~12 Zircon hypersonic cruise missiles launched, 0 intercepted. ~6 Kalibr cruise missiles launched, 6 intercepted. ~2 Kh-59/69 cruise missiles launched, 2 intercepted. ~74 missiles total, ~24 intercepted (~6/24 ballistics, ~18/50 cruise missiles). Air defence performed far more poorly this attack compared to the previous ones, despite still having quite a few Patriot interceptors. It seems that a large portion of the Patriot PAC-3 interceptors were wasted on trying to intercept Zircons, which are much harder to shoot down than Iskander-Ms. F-16s, Mirage-2000s, and IRIS-T interceptors worked quite well on the Kalibrs. They also did decently well east of Kyiv considering the fact that so many missiles were flying in at once, which overwhelmed air defence. However, the overall interception rate was far lower this time. These above figures are not final and will be further refined in the coming hours. Ukraine is working toward a just peace. Meanwhile, Russia, having failed to achieve its goals on the battlefield, is intensifying strikes on Ukrainian cities. Overnight, the enemy carried out one of the largest attacks on Ukraine: nearly 500 strike drones and 77 missiles, including 25 ballistic or hypersonic missiles. Thanks to the professionalism of our warriors and the support of our partners, more than 90% of cruise missiles and 90% of Shahed-type strike drones were intercepted. We thank our air defense forces, who protect Ukrainian skies every day and every night. At the same time, intercepting ballistic missiles remains a key challenge due to a shortage of missiles for Patriot systems. To secure the country with anti-ballistic missiles, in April the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine signed its first record contract for hundreds of PAC-2 missiles for Patriot, with Germany's support. Deliveries will begin over the coming years. For the first time, a step has also been taken toward purchasing around one hundred Patriot missiles worth $1 billion, financed through an EU loan. This year, Ukraine also began receiving missiles from European partners' stockpiles for the first time. In addition, through the implementation of the NATO After Action Review standard, Patriot effectiveness against maneuvering Iskander missiles has already more than doubled. But this is not enough — Ukraine critically needs additional missiles for its Patriot systems. They are available in partners' stockpiles. The protection of Ukrainian skies depends on fast decisions, the scaling of the PURL mechanism, and missile procurement through JUMPSTART. Ukraine's Minister of Defence has already sent letters to nearly 40 partner nations requesting the urgent transfer of Patriot missiles from existing stocks to Ukraine this month — in exchange for future deliveries already contracted for Ukraine. The Minister has also called on partners to contribute to the PURL and JUMPSTART mechanisms. These are the fastest and most reliable ways to supply the Patriot missiles Ukraine needs. It is critically important that decisions be made now, ahead of the NATO summit. The speed of our partners' decisions directly determines the protection of Ukrainian skies, critical infrastructure, and the lives of our people.

Türkiye’s Health Minister Prof Dr Kemal Memişoğlu and I signed the Istanbul Outcome Statement following the Ministerial Conference on advancing health security through earthquake emergency management. The statement calls on countries and partners to turn lessons into readiness people can count on: knowing the risks before earthquakes strike; preparing hospitals and clinics to keep essential services running; training and supporting emergency teams; and strengthening cooperation across sectors and borders so that care reaches people quickly and fairly. That call felt especially real as we heard from Mr Murat Genc, a volunteer from Türkiye’s National Medical Rescue Team (UMKE), who joined us online from Venezuela. His words showed what preparedness and solidarity mean in practice: trained teams reaching people when lives depend on fast, coordinated action. After the signing, Minister Memişoğlu and I joined UMKE volunteers for a photo, a powerful reminder that this agenda is ultimately about people ready to serve when others need them most. Microsoft is just one beneficiary of 250 years of American history and the choices made by past generations. As an American company, we believe we have a responsibility to understand where we have been, learn from it, and help make real for others the opportunities created for us. As America enters its 251st year, we face another inflection point shaped by rapid technological change. That is why we created this series. Throughout July, we will reflect on moments in American history with six video episodes when people faced uncertainty and made choices that set in motion consequences they could not fully see. Some decisions advanced the country. Others revealed how much work remained. Together, they remind us that history is not inevitable; it is made by people, in moments, through choices. Our goal is not simply to celebrate that history, but to learn and connect the past to the questions we face today. John Adams, writing to Abigail, about the Continental Congress' vote in favor of independence on July 2, 1776: "The Second Day of July 1776, will be the most memorable Epocha, in the History of America. I am apt to believe that it will be celebrated, by succeeding Generations, as the great anniversary Festival. It ought to be commemorated, as the Day of Deliverance by solemn Acts of Devotion to God Almighty. It ought to be solemnized with Pomp and Parade, with Shews, Games, Sports, Guns, Bells, Bonfires and Illuminations from one End of this Continent to the other from this Time forward forever more. You will think me transported with Enthusiasm but I am not. -- I am well aware of the Toil and Blood and Treasure, that it will cost Us to maintain this Declaration, and support and defend these States. -- Yet through all the Gloom I can see the Rays of ravishing Light and Glory. I can see that the End is more than worth all the Means. And that Posterity will tryumph in that Days Transaction, even altho We should rue it, which I trust in God We shall not."

If social media posts of Judge Hamayoun Dilawar are authentic (Tosha Khana Case Judge), this is alarming and raises serious and reasonable doubts on credibility of trial being conducted by him. In my view, propriety demands that he should immediately recuse or disassociate himself from the case. It needs to be noted that Seven Member Bench of the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Malik Qayyum Case (reported in 2001 PLD SC 568) held that bias on part of the judge vitiates judicial proceedings. The court further held that an accused has a right of a fair trial by a judicial minded person, not by someone functioning under an influence or bias as the same paralyses his judicial faculties to conduct fair trial. Bias would vitiate judicial proceedings if such circumstances exist. Bias robs the judge of the confidence that a litigant may have in the judge. Court further held that bias is mental disposition or attitude towards a particular person and covers all kind of hostilities and prejudices against him.

Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, and Prof. K. V. Raju, Member, NITI Aayog, participated in a panel discussion on "Data, Statistics and India's Growth Agenda", held as part of "Swarna Andhra @ 2047: Economic Intelligence for Governance", a two-day capacity-building programme organised by the Planning Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh. The panel was moderated by Shri Suresh Goyal, Director General, NCAER, and featured Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI; Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Adviser, Government of India; and Prof. S. Mahendra Dev, Chairman, EAC-PM, as fellow panellists. Dr. Balasubramaniam emphasised that data must serve as a foundation for dignity in governance, making visible those often overlooked in averages, including informal workers and tribal communities. He noted that while India already has rich individual-level data, the priority now is to harmonise datasets across ministries, break institutional silos, and use evidence to strengthen social development and citizen capability. As India advances towards Viksit Bharat, he stressed that better decisions depend on engaging with what the data truly reveals and viewing citizens as active participants in the development journey. In a major international effort to evaluate potential treatments for #Ebola disease due to Bundibugyo virus (BVD), the PARTNERS (Platform Adaptive Randomised Trial for New and Repurposed Filovirus TreatmentS) clinical trial has opened enrolment today for patients in the #DRC. What does the trial do? This trial will assess whether two therapies – ➡️ a monoclonal antibody (MBP134) ➡️ an antiviral medicine (remdesivir) can improve survival among people diagnosed with BVD. It will also evaluate whether combining the two provides additional benefits. Who is behind it? "Yesterday, President @EmmanuelMacron of #France and I published a joint op-ed about the impact of #SocialMedia and other digital environments on the health of young people. In the past year, several governments including Australia, Canada, France, Indonesia, Ireland, Spain and the United Kingdom have all introduced measures to protect children from online harm. Together, these measures reflect a growing global consensus that digital environments require effective governance, accountability, age-appropriate design, and stronger safeguards to protect child health. Digital environments are not neutral. How they are designed, governed, and monetized shapes many aspects of our lives, including health. For example, repeated exposure to stereotyped, sexualized, violent, or discriminatory content shapes how children understand themselves and the world around them. It can also lead children to make unrealistic comparisons with others, undermining their confidence and self-esteem. Algorithms increasingly filter health information to increase attention and engagement rather than accuracy, allowing misleading claims to spread. And features including infinite scrolling, auto-play, personalized content and push notifications increase the risk for addictive behaviour. The collection and use of personal data, particularly for profiling and targeted marketing, raise concerns about privacy, manipulation, and well-being. WHO is responding to these concerns by strengthening research, advising countries, and promoting safe, equitable digital health environments. Preventing exposure to illegal or extreme and graphic content is essential. But children’s well-being requires more than the absence of harm. It depends on stable relationships, appropriate boundaries, physical activity, and opportunities for real-world social connection. Above all, we must listen to young people. They are not experimental subjects, a captive market, or a commodity. They are our future. Together, we can – and must – shape digital environments that protect and support their health"-@DrTedros nitter.perennialte.ch/DrTedros/status/207226… Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus (@DrTedros) Digital spaces bring opportunities, but also risks for children’s health and development.
